Hermes.//: One independent Hermes gateway per agent. HomeHub chooses an AGENT; Hermes owns model,
Hermes.//_2: provider, tier, routing, escalation, fallback, vision and locality. No model name here, ever.
Hermes.//_3: Loopback is deliberate: the API key has no route-level scoping, so the gateways are not on
Hermes.//_4: the LAN. HomeHub must therefore share the host network namespace with Hermes.
Hermes.//_5: Keys are secrets: dotnet user-secrets set "Hermes:Agents:barnaby:ApiKey" "<key>"

//AllowedHosts: Host-header filter (AUDIT A6). Deliberately left at * here and set per deployment instead:
the panel is reached by IP, by hostname, and by <name>.local over mDNS, and which of those a
household uses is not knowable from this file. A wrong value is not a subtle failure - every
request answers 400 and the panel is simply gone, including the health check that would have
told you why. Narrow it in /etc/homehub/homehub.env once the real names are known:

OpenFoodFacts.//: Barcode -> product name for the pantry scanner. Open data, no API key. The pantry's only
OpenFoodFacts.//_2: call off the LAN: it sends a barcode and nothing else. Set Enabled false to turn every
OpenFoodFacts.//_3: outbound lookup off — scanning still works, each new pack just needs naming once.
